messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — since the kernel bump on the GPU fleet last night we're seeing repeated gRPC stream stalls between pods on different nodes. Small requests are fine, but streams with large payloads stall mid-stream and later recover with retransmits.

maria: Hmm. Sounds like MTU / offload mismatch to me. Can you grab `ip link show` on node and `ip link show` inside pod netns + a quick `ping -s 2000 -M do` to the peer pod IP?

sanjay: Pasted quick outputs below from node-a and a pod (see timestamps). Not a full capture but should show weird MTU bits.

node-a$ ip link show eth0
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 3c:97:0e:aa:bb:cc brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff

node-a$ ip link show vxlan0
10: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default

pod ns (vethXYZ) $ ip link show vethXYZ
3: vethXYZ@if4: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default

pod->pod ping -s 2000 -M do 10.2.5.18
PING 10.2.5.18 (10.2.5.18) 2000(2028) bytes of data.
From 10.2.4.11 icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1452)
From 10.2.4.11 icmp_seq=2 Frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1452)
--- 10.2.5.18 ping statistics ---
2 packets transmitted, 0 received, +2 errors, 100% packet loss, time 1002ms

maria: There we go — ICMP Frag-needed with mtu 1452. Looks like tunnel overhead not accounted for. But vxlan shows 9000 on node while veths/pods are 1500 and underlying eth0 is 1500. Something is translating wrong OR large GSO packets are getting past the kernel and dropped on the physical switch.

devin: Any kernel/gso/gro/tso changes in the update? I remember an upstream change that toggled generic segmentation on some NIC drivers. Also check ethtool offloads on the physical NIC and the veth.

sanjay: Quick ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0: 
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on (anonymous)
scatter-gather: on
segmentation-offload: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on

And ethtool -k vethXYZ shows tso/gso/gro on as well.

ops-jen: infra-bot reports that the kernel package roll included qed driver 7.15.x which flips a hw offload setting by default. See pkg:kernel-5.15.0-167. Change log: "enable tx-gso by default for qed".

maria: That matches — packets are being coalesced into large segments (GSO) on the host, the vxlan tunnel reduces MTU and an intermediate switch with 1500 drops the oversized frames. gRPC streaming uses long messages and the stream stalls because retransmits happen and TCP stacks struggle with partial segments.

devin: Short term mitigation: enable tcp_mtu_probing and disable GSO on the veths connecting pods so the kernel emits properly sized segments. Also set pod overlay mtu to 1452 (or whatever ping showed). Commands: 

sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
for i in $(ip -o link show | awk -F: '{print $2}' | grep veth); do ethtool -K $i gso off gro off tso off || true; done
# update CNI config: "mtu": 1452 for vxlan/overlay

sanjay: Tried the tcp_mtu_probing + disable GSO patch on one node; the stream held steady for 30m during load test. I also set the CNI overlay mtu to 1452 cluster-wide and kicked a rolling restart; initial results look good.

maria: Longer term we should:
- Align upstream docs for the kernel change and our kernel packaging.
- Add a post-up check in node bootstrap that validates overlay mtu vs physical mtu and fails fast if mismatch.
- Add automatic ethtool offload toggles for veths when kernel flips default.

devin: Filed INFRA-2379 to track automation + a canary rollout for kernel packages. Add a runbook snippet: how to detect (ping -M do, check Frag needed), quickfix (ethtool -K veth gso off), and recommended permanent fix (CNI mtu + kernel packaging rollback or driver config).

infra-bot: Deploy bot: Rollout kernel-5.15.0-167 marked as paused in canary (reason: net offload regressions). See https://deploys.redwood.internal/rollouts/2379

ops-jen: tagging @oncall for awareness, will monitor network metrics dashboard for packet drops and gRPC error spikes for next 4 hours. :eyes:
